title: The Painted Inheritance
premise: True-crime podcaster Bram Marchetti reopens the thirty-year-old Hollis Gallery murders, a case closed on a confession from a man who later recanted and died in prison. When a fresh body surfaces wearing clothes lifted from Bram's own closet, staged like a scene from his unreleased episode drafts, he realizes the killer has access to his files, his home, and his past. As the killer reenacts the original murders with Bram cast as both witness and suspect, Bram uncovers that the 'confessed' man was framed by a powerful family whose anniversary dinner will celebrate their patriarch's legacy. At the dinner, Bram exposes the surviving conspirator with a trap built from the killer's own obsession with the case file, ending with justice served outside the law and Bram choosing to broadcast the truth rather than protect himself.
about_author: Felix Ravensworth is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing trials before turning to fiction, giving his thrillers an ear for the exact moment testimony cracks. He lives in a coastal town he refuses to name, citing an unsolved case he swears he'll write about someday.

chapters.title: The Coldest File
chapters.summary: Bram Marchetti, in his own wry first-person voice, introduces his podcast and his perfect record of closed cases as he pulls the Hollis Gallery murders from a stack of cold files. A recanted confession, a dead defendant, a wealthy family untouched. The emotional beat is restless ambition: Bram smells an ending no one else could find.

chapters.title: Clothes That Weren't Mine
chapters.summary: Detective Odile Ferran calls Bram to a riverside crime scene where the victim wears Bram's own missing jacket and scarf. POV shifts to Ferran's cool procedural third person. Bram's confidence cracks into unease as he realizes the staging quotes his unpublished episode outline beat for beat.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Bram interviews the original case's surviving witness, elderly archivist Mirabel Quist, who remembers more than her 1994 statement allowed. Flashback threads introduce the Hollis family and their patriarch Aldous. The beat is creeping dread: the past isn't cold, it's waiting.

chapters.title: The Man Who Confessed
chapters.summary: Bram digs into Danny Voss, the handyman who confessed, recanted, and died in prison. Through prison letters and a surviving sister's grief, Bram becomes convinced Voss was framed. Emotional beat: guilt, as Bram realizes his earlier teaser episode may have helped bury Voss's name.

chapters.title: Someone Read My Drafts
chapters.summary: Ferran's POV: forensics show the killer had access to Bram's cloud-stored drafts, and a break-in at Bram's studio reveals files copied, nothing stolen. Bram's paranoia sharpens. The beat is violation, the hunter learning he was always the hunted.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Invitation
chapters.summary: An engraved invitation arrives for the Hollis family's legacy dinner, signed by a hand Bram recognizes from a forged letter in the old case file. POV returns to Bram, now certain the killer is toying with him. The beat is dark fascination: the trap has an RSVP.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Kept
chapters.summary: Mirabel gives Bram a hidden ledger from the gallery, records of art sales used to launder money for the family. Her fear is palpable; she's been silent for thirty years to stay alive. The beat is fragile courage, a witness finally choosing a side.

chapters.title: Second Scene, Staged for Me
chapters.summary: A second murder recreates the gallery's back room, with a Polaroid of Bram's front door left at the scene. Ferran's POV tightens the noose: officially, Bram is now a person of interest. The beat is claustrophobia, the investigation turning inward.

chapters.title: The Sister's Testimony
chapters.summary: Voss's sister, Lena, gives Bram Danny's letters describing pressure from a family lawyer. Bram airs a mid-season episode naming the Hollises, burning his careful neutrality. The beat is righteous fury tempered by fear of what he's provoked.

chapters.title: A Killer Who Quotes
chapters.summary: The killer contacts Bram directly through an old tip line, reciting case-file details only the original investigators knew. Bram realizes the killer may be one of them, or someone raised on their secrets. The beat is intellectual dread, matching wits with a mind built from the same documents.

chapters.title: The Understudy
chapters.summary: Ferran discovers the original lead detective, now retired and dying, took hush money to close the case fast. His deathbed half-confession points to the family's lawyer, Corwin Hale. The beat is bitter vindication: the rot was institutional.

chapters.title: House of Hollis
chapters.summary: Bram goes undercover at a Hollis charity gala, mapping the family: the brittle widow, the heir with a drinking problem, the quietly brilliant daughter-in-law Sable. The beat is predatory elegance, everyone smiling over something buried.

chapters.title: Sable Knows
chapters.summary: Sable Hollis corners Bram, revealing she's been reading his podcast to understand her husband's family, and she has her own suspicions about the anniversary dinner. Uneasy alliance forms. The beat is wary intimacy between two investigators of the same house.

chapters.title: Erased
chapters.summary: Mirabel's apartment burns the night after Bram's visit; she survives but vanishes, and the ledger is gone. Ferran's POV: the killer is cleaning house, and every lead now runs through Bram. The beat is grief and self-reproach, his investigation painting targets.

chapters.title: The File Within the File
chapters.summary: Bram reconstructs the killer's pattern: each murder corrects an 'error' in the original investigation, as if the killer is editing the case to a truer version. He realizes the final scene will be the anniversary dinner itself. The beat is terrible clarity, the shape of the ending revealed.

chapters.title: Ferran's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Ferran, ordered to arrest Bram on mounting circumstantial evidence, instead shows him the warrant and gives him until the dinner. Her quiet rebellion costs her professionally. The beat is trust extended across institutional lines, justice choosing its instruments.

chapters.title: What Bram Buried
chapters.summary: Bram confronts his own secret: years ago he quietly killed a story that would have exposed the Hollises, trading integrity for access. He confesses it on air. The beat is painful self-honesty, the podcaster becoming a subject of his own show.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Set
chapters.summary: Using the killer's obsession with the case file, Bram plants a doctored 'final draft' implying Mirabel's ledger survives in his studio, forcing the killer to come to him before the dinner. The beat is cold resolve, the invisible man making himself bait.

chapters.title: The Editor Revealed
chapters.summary: The killer is caught in Bram's studio: Sable's husband, Julian, the family's overlooked archivist who discovered the murders as a boy and has been 'correcting' the record ever since. His monologue is chillingly reasonable. The beat is horrified recognition of a kindred obsessive.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Julian escapes custody and attends the dinner to complete the final scene: killing the patriarch's heir as the 'last correction.' Bram and Ferran intervene; Julian dies falling from the gallery balcony among the paintings he meant to avenge. The beat is chaos and grief, justice arriving bloodied.

chapters.title: Outside the Law
chapters.summary: With Julian dead, the legal case against the Hollises collapses, so Bram broadcasts the full evidence, the ledger's contents, the bribes, Voss's innocence, and lets the public do what the courts wouldn't. Ferran quietly reopens the official file. The beat is defiant catharsis.

chapters.title: The Last Episode
chapters.summary: Epilogue in Bram's voice: the Hollis estate is dissolved, Voss's name is cleared posthumously, and Mirabel, found alive, records her own testimony for the finale. Bram closes the case, then opens a new file, changed. The beat is hard-won peace and a promise to keep listening.
